pricing.freeTierCaps: 3 total site slots on Carrd-branded URLs; no custom domains, forms, embeds/widgets or analytics
pricing.billingTerms: annual only for Pro plans; optional automatic yearly renewal or manual pay-as-you-go renewal
pricing.hiddenCosts: The low-cost Lite plans do not support custom domains or business features; higher site-slot variants increase the annual price, and account credits/virtual balance are non-cash and non-transferable.

verdictSummary: A one-page static site generator with forms and custom domains is absolutely vibecodable; Carrd's price is so low that DIY only makes sense for control or learning.
coreLoopDIY: Generate/edit a single-page HTML site from blocks, host it, attach a domain, and optionally send forms to email/webhook.
whatYouLose: not having to think about hosting
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the product costs almost nothing and removes all hosting/domain friction.

priorArt.name: GrapesJS
priorArt.desc: Open-source web builder library; enough to build a simple Carrd-like editor.

alternatives.name: Mobirise AI
alternatives.desc: Three generated and exportable sites a month for free; the templates retain a faint Bootstrap aftertaste.

facts.install: Browser signup; projects can be hosted by Mobirise or exported as HTML, CSS and JavaScript
facts.engines: Proprietary text-to-site, copy, image and video generation; the underlying model providers are not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Projects are saved in the hosted builder; export downloads ordinary HTML, CSS, JavaScript and asset files
facts.gapVsPaid: Mobirise AI is less minimal and predictable than Carrd for a single page, with a three-new-sites-per-month free cap.
facts.setupBlocker: The permanent free allowance is capped at three distinct generated/exported projects per month

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: A custom-domain visual site on the free plan; comically overpowered for a one-page profile and branded accordingly.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optional npm-installed Plasmic CLI for React code generation and deployment in your own repository
facts.engines: Plasmic AI (beta); the official site does not name its underlying model provider
facts.dataFormat: Hosted projects and CMS records in Plasmic Cloud; codegen writes React components plus plasmic.json and plasmic.lock into the user's repository
facts.gapVsPaid: For a one-page profile, Plasmic is far more complex than Carrd and its free hosted result keeps a platform badge.
facts.setupBlocker: Free hosted output keeps Plasmic branding; codegen/self-deployment requires a Node/React project and deployment workflow

alternatives.name: Silex
alternatives.desc: A visual one-page builder that exports plain HTML and costs nothing; publishing begins with a GitLab login.

facts.install: Use the hosted editor with a GitLab login, install the desktop alpha, or run the official Docker setup
facts.engines: Optional desktop MCP workflow can connect to Ollama, OpenCode, Goose or Claude Code
facts.dataFormat: Project JSON and assets in GitLab, FTP or local storage; publishing produces ordinary static HTML, CSS and JavaScript
facts.gapVsPaid: Silex creates more publishing and layout work than Carrd's extremely simple one-page workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The stable hosted route starts with a GitLab account; the desktop build is still labelled alpha

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Three hosted funnels and a custom domain free; perfect when the one-page site is secretly collecting leads.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, funnels, course/community content, orders, emails and uploaded files in systeme.io's vendor-managed cloud; the underlying storage format is not published
facts.gapVsPaid: systeme.io is a funnel platform with much less visual control than Carrd, so a simple profile page inherits marketing-oriented structure.
facts.setupBlocker: Selling requires connecting a payment gateway; the free plan is capped at 2,000 contacts, three funnels, one course, one community and one custom domain

alternatives.name: Webstudio
alternatives.desc: Far more CSS control than Carrd and far more self-hosting responsibility.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; alternatively export the project or deploy the self-hosted builder/site
facts.engines: Webstudio Inception AI and MCP integrations; the hosted model provider is not named in official documentation
facts.dataFormat: Projects and assets live in Webstudio Cloud when hosted there; export/self-host routes produce source or static assets under the user's deployment
facts.gapVsPaid: Webstudio is overpowered for a one-page site and makes a free custom domain a hosting/deployment task.
facts.setupBlocker: The free cloud plan publishes only to a Webstudio subdomain; a free custom domain requires export or self-hosting

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A library for creating builders, not the one-page builder a normal person came to install.

notes: To be fair, Carrd is famously cheap. But you have Claude Code; you don't need a site builder at all.
prompt:
Build me a one-page personal site to replace Carrd. Requirements:

- One elegant single-page site from a content.json file: name, headline, short
  about paragraph, avatar, social links, and an optional list of projects with
  title + description + URL. Editing the JSON is the CMS.
- Design it properly: strong typographic hierarchy, generous whitespace, one
  accent color set via a CSS variable, dark mode via prefers-color-scheme,
  tasteful hover states. It should look designed, not templated.
- A working contact form with no third-party service: POST to a tiny endpoint
  that appends to messages.log and returns an inline thank-you. Honeypot field
  for bots.
- Perfect Lighthouse scores: inline the CSS, no frameworks, no webfonts unless
  self-hosted, proper OG tags + generated OG image.
- Static HTML + one small server file for the form. Deploy instructions for
  any VPS or static host + serverless form alternative.
